full_text_en:
China Pacific Insurance Co., Ltd., Dalian Branch v. Dalian Yangfan Shipping Co., Ltd. — retrial of dispute over return of guarantee

Applicant for Retrial: China Pacific Insurance Co., Ltd., Dalian Branch
Legal Representative: Xu Jinghui, General Manager

Counterparty: Dalian Yangfan Shipping Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Li Bingkui, General Manager

With respect to the case of dispute over return of guarantee between the applicant for retrial, China Pacific Insurance Co., Ltd., Dalian Branch (hereinafter referred to as Dalian Pacific Insurance), and the counterparty, Dalian Yangfan Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yangfan Company), the Dalian Maritime Court rendered a civil ruling (1997) Dahai Fa Zai Zi No. 1 on September 9, 1997, which has become legally effective. Dalian Pacific Insurance, dissatisfied with the aforesaid ruling, filed an application for retrial with the Supreme People's Court on the ground that Yangfan Company failed to institute an action in court within 30 days after applying for the arrest of the ship, and therefore the guarantee letter provided by Dalian Pacific Insurance should be returned. It requested the revocation of the ruling of the Dalian Maritime Court that recognized it as the surety for the collision liability compensation of the vessel "Suchun."

The Supreme People's Court found upon retrial:

On February 8, 1994, after a collision dispute arose between the counterparty Yangfan Company and the owner of the St. Vincent-flagged vessel "Suchun," Yangfan Company applied to the Dalian Maritime Court for the arrest of the "Suchun." On the same day, the Dalian Maritime Court ruled to arrest the "Suchun" in Dalian Port and ordered the owner of the "Suchun" to provide a guarantee. The owner of the "Suchun" then provided to Yangfan Company a guarantee letter of USD 60,000 issued by the applicant for retrial, Dalian Pacific Insurance. Based on that, Yangfan Company applied to the court for the release of the "Suchun." The next day, the Dalian Maritime Court issued an order to release the arrested ship.

On July 7, 1994, the counterparty Yangfan Company filed an action in the Dalian Maritime Court claiming compensation for collision losses from the owner of the "Suchun." On September 13, the Dalian Maritime Court notified Dalian Pacific Insurance to participate in the proceedings as a third party. On September 20, the owner of the "Suchun" filed an application with the Dalian Maritime Court, requesting the court to return the guarantee letter it had provided on the ground that "Yangfan Company failed to institute an action within 30 days, exceeding the statutory time limit." On October 6, the Dalian Maritime Court rendered the ruling (1994) Dahai Fa Shi Bao Zi No. 4-3, ruling to return the guarantee letter provided by the owner of the "Suchun" and simultaneously notifying Dalian Pacific Insurance to withdraw from the proceedings.

On October 28, 1996, Yangfan Company filed an application for retrial on the ground that "the Supreme People's Court's provisions on arrest of ships do not contain provisions for the return of guarantees, and the No. 4-3 ruling of the Dalian Maritime Court was erroneous in the application of law." After retrial, the Dalian Maritime Court held that Dalian Pacific Insurance, as the surety for collision compensation of the "Suchun," should bear the suretyship liability. The return of Dalian Pacific Insurance's guarantee by the No. 4-3 ruling was an erroneous application of law. Accordingly, the retrial ruling revoked the No. 4-3 ruling.

The Supreme People's Court held:

Article 251, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that an interested party in a case involving foreign elements may apply to the people's court for property preservation before instituting an action. Pre-litigation arrest of a ship is a pre-litigation property preservation measure taken by a maritime court upon the application of a maritime claimant. Article 4, Item (4) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Arrest of Ships Prior to Litigation by Maritime Courts (hereinafter referred to as the 1994 Arrest Provisions), issued on July 6, 1994, provides: "Where the respondent provides a guarantee as ordered by the maritime court, and such guarantee is accepted by the maritime court, or the applicant applies for the release of the arrest order for justified reasons, the maritime court shall promptly issue an order to release the arrested ship." It can be seen from this that the guarantee relationship between the applicant for the arrest of the ship and the respondent is formed under the intervention of state coercive force.

Article 252 of the Civil Procedure Law provides: "After the people's court rules to permit pre-litigation property preservation, the applicant shall institute an action within thirty days. If the applicant fails to do so within the time limit, the people's court shall discharge the property preservation." The counterparty Yangfan Company applied for the arrest of the ship on February 8, 1994, and was immediately granted permission by the Dalian Maritime Court, but the company did not institute an action until July 7 of the same year, which exceeded the time limit. Pursuant to the provisions of the law, the property preservation in this case should be discharged.

The order to release the arrested ship issued by the Dalian Maritime Court in accordance with Article 4, Item (4) of the 1994 Arrest Provisions is not the discharge of property preservation as provided in Article 252 of the Civil Procedure Law. Because the guarantee letter on file replaced the arrested ship, the ship was released. At that point, although the property preservation implemented in the form of ship arrest was discharged, the property preservation implemented in the form of a guarantee was not discharged. For the applicant for ship arrest to maintain the effect of the property preservation implemented in the form of a guarantee, it must institute an action within the statutory time limit. If no action is instituted within the time limit, the property preservation implemented in the form of a guarantee shall also be discharged according to law, and the guarantee letter shall be returned to the guarantor.

In summary, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 177, Paragraph 2 and Article 179, Paragraph 1, Item 3 of the Civil Procedure Law, rendered the following ruling on November 16, 1998:

1. Revoke the civil ruling (1997) Dahai Fa Zai Zi No. 1 of the Dalian Maritime Court;
2. Uphold the civil ruling (1994) Dahai Fa Shi Bao Zi No. 4-3 of the Dalian Maritime Court.
